name: number-gets-its-bar
style: late-90s New York street rap, one heavyset MC who treats his verse like a bebop drum solo turned into words: rhythm played as melody, syllables dragged a hair behind the snare then tumbled out in loose clusters, stacked multisyllable rhymes rolling into each other, unbothered talking cadence, a deliberate beat of silence right before each punchline lands. Vocal: enormous man, low velvet chest baritone, lazy Brooklyn vowels, a short asthmatic wheeze audible on every inhale, dry and right on the mic. Instrumental: 88 BPM, swung dusty breakbeat with a thick knocking kick and a hard flat snare, a melancholy after-midnight Rhodes-and-organ soul-jazz figure sliced into a cold, menacing minor loop, walking acoustic-bass-style bottom end, tape hiss and crackle; a hoarse sampled crowd-chant voice shouts each number alone, then one empty bar of drums and loop, the MC starting his line only on the next downbeat; bare, minimal, threatening, no hook
exclude: double-time flow, rushed delivery, sung chorus, female vocals, autotune, trap hi-hats, 808 rolls
lyrics:
[Intro]
Uh. Money printer manual. Take notes.

[Rule One]
[sampled shout: the number, then one bare bar of beat]
Rule number Uno: never say how much you made,
doesn't matter anyway, since the gold went away.

[Rule Two]
[sampled shout: the number, then one bare bar of beat]
Number two: never show 'em your next move,
cut the rate for the banks, hike it when you land.

[Rule Three]
[sampled shout: the number, then one bare bar of beat]
Number three: never trust nobody with the press,
before Bernie gets made off face loss.

[Rule Four]
[sampled shout: the number, then one bare bar of beat]
Number four: never get high on your own supply,
banks took the first hit, now the rent's sky-high.

[Rule Five]
[sampled shout: the number, then one bare bar of beat]
Number five: never print where you sleep,
never let them owe the oats you reap.

[Rule Six]
[sampled shout: the number, then one bare bar of beat]
Number six: no credit? Forget it,
let the junkie know you better forget that.

[Rule Seven]
[sampled shout: the number, then one bare bar of beat]
Seven, and nobody says it out loud:
keep your money and your assets apart, not in one crowd.

[Rule Eight]
[sampled shout: the number, then one bare bar of beat]
Number eight: hold none of it yourself,
debase 'em till the numbers go through.

[Rule Nine]
[sampled shout: the number, then one bare bar of beat]
Nine's the one they'd rather you skipped:
keep the auditors out, sporadic trips and you out.

[Rule Ten]
[sampled shout: the number, then one bare bar of beat]
Number ten: no consignment, cash up front, that's law,
they took the bailout in stride and they ain't paid it all.

[Outro]
[one bare bar of beat, then the MC]
And the fix, from the future? No hand on the printer.

[Instrumental: beat rides out, two bars, then stops]
